info.name: KeeNext
info.summary: Alpha: open and edit KeePass (KDBX) password databases stored in your Nextcloud
info.description:
**Alpha software.** KeeNext is under active development and has not been independently audited. It is provided as is, without warranty and without liability. Keep your own backups of every database you open with it, and do not make it the only copy of your passwords.
Open and edit KeePass databases (.kdbx) directly in Nextcloud, compatible with KeePassXC, KeePass and KeePassDX.
- Databases are decrypted only in your browser; the server never sees your master password or the contents. - Open `.kdbx` files from the Files app with a click, or from the app with the file picker and a list of recently opened databases. - Changes made elsewhere (KeePassXC through the desktop client, another browser) are merged instead of overwritten. - KDBX 3.1 and 4.x, Argon2d/Argon2id, AES-KDF, AES, ChaCha20 and Twofish, key files. - Groups, search with KeePassXC syntax, entry history, attachments, TOTP, password generator.
**Network requests.** Nothing about your databases is sent to third parties. Two features you start yourself contact other servers: the breach check in the health report sends the first 5 characters of each password's SHA-1 hash from your browser to api.pwnedpasswords.com, and downloading an entry's favicon makes your Nextcloud server request the icon from that entry's website.
info.author: Jan-Hendrik Meyer
